facts.text: edge_follow-v0 is registered with entry point tactile_gym.rl_envs.exploration.edge_follow.edge_follow_env:EdgeFollowEnv
EdgeFollowEnv computes a simulation time step of 1/240 s, a control rate of 1/10 s and a velocity action repeat of floor(control_rate / sim_time_step)
The EdgeFollowEnv constructor's default max_steps is 250
The termination distance to the goal is 0.01 m
The mg400 branch sets the TCP limits x -0.150 to +0.150, y -0.11 to +0.11, z -0.1 to +0.1, roll and pitch 0 to 0 and yaw -pi to +pi
The action space is a Box with low=min_action, high=max_action and shape (act_dim,)
get_act_dim returns 2 when movement_mode is xy
The oracle observation concatenates the TCP position, the TCP linear velocity, the goal position and the edge angle
The dense reward is -((1.0 * goal_dist) + (10.0 * edge_dist) + (1.0 * yaw_dist)) with yaw_dist 0
The edge angle is drawn uniformly from -pi to pi on every reset
The edge length is 0.105 for mg400/magician and 0.175 for the other arms, and the edge height is 0.035
The observation space for observation_mode oracle is a Dict with one Box from -inf to +inf whose shape is the oracle observation shape
step returns (observation, reward, done, {}) - the legacy Gym API four-tuple, not the Gymnasium five-tuple
seed sets the environment RNG through gym.utils.seeding.np_random
close disconnects PyBullet and destroys the OpenCV windows

determinism.notes: reset(seed=...) or cap.world.seed.v1 fixes the fake's edge angle and start state through Python's random.Random; upstream draws them with numpy's gym seeding generator, so one seed does not give the same trajectory on the two implementations

gaps: the fake backend is a pure Python 2-D kinematic stand-in for the PyBullet environment: it mirrors the public reset/seed/step/close surface and the two spaces, integrates the TCP at the control rate and computes the upstream dense reward from the goal and edge distances; it runs no rigid-body dynamics, contacts, robot arm IK or PyBullet physics
the fake draws the edge angle and initial state with Python's random.Random; upstream draws them with numpy's generator, so a seed does not repeat the same trajectory on the two implementations
the observation is the 10-value oracle vector only; the tactile image, visual image and extended feature observation modes are not modelled, and no tactile sensor is simulated
the upstream environment is PyBullet rigid-body dynamics (F1); this package declares F0 because the fake integrates no dynamics and was never compared with the upstream environment
no wall-clock pacing: realtime_factor 0, one bridge tick advances one control interval of 0.1 s, which upstream splits into 24 physics steps of 1/240 s
the sim backend (gym.make('edge_follow-v0')) needs PyBullet, OpenCV, numpy and an import of tactile_gym.rl_envs so the id is registered; it was not run here
snapshot and restore are not offered: the environment exposes no get_state/set_state pair
no physical robot arm or tactile sensor is modelled and nothing was validated against hardware

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the environment state is kept and stays readable
